newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: ISLAMIC BANK APPROVES $196.5 MLN IN FINANCING.
newsitem.headline: ISLAMIC BANK APPROVES $196.5 MLN IN FINANCING.

text.p: The Islamic Development Bank (IDB) said on Thursday it had approved financing facilities worth $196.5 million to member states.

An IDB statement said the bank would finance five development projects in five member countries worth $80.5 million, seven foreign trade operations in five states worth $100.7 million and two financing operations worth $15.3 million.
Iran would receive $44 million, of which $29 million would go towards purchasing equipment for a sugar plant and $15 million to import spare parts for diesel locomotives and passenger coaches.

Pakistan would get $32.8 million to import crude oil from Saudi Arabia and finance a power project. Turkey will receive $30 million to import steel scrap, Indonesia $23.5 million to finance three power distribution control centres and Tunisia $20.7 million to finance imports of coke, iron ore, zinc and ferroalloys and buy paper pulp and chemical products.

The bank said it would give Mozambique $11 million to finance a road project, Bangladesh $10 million to finance a power project, Egypt $10 million to import ferro-manganese, Mali $7 million for an airport project and $7.5 million for Saudi Arabia's Jamjoom Pharmaceutical Factory.
The 50-member IDB was set up in 1975 to promote trade exchanges between Islamic states.
